newsitem.title: INDIA: Sluggish overseas buying cuts Indian castor prices.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish overseas buying cuts Indian castor prices.

text.p: Indian castorseed June delivery prices on Wednesday fell to 1,186/1,187 rupees per quintal from 1,201/1,202 rupees on the back of fresh speculative selling, dealers said.
"Castorseed arrivals however remained low but sluggish overseas buying and tight money conditions ahead of the financial year-end prompted fresh bull liquidation," a dealer said.
The financial year closes on March 31. Arrivals of castorseed in the Gujarat region remained low at 4,000/5,000 bags (75 kg each) against the daily average of 25,000/30,000 bags last week.
"Lower arrivals may help June delivery to bounce back again," the dealer said.

Groundnut oil rose to 349/350 rupees from 343/345 rupees per 10 kg on limited arrivals of 40/50 tonnes coupled with renewed seasonal support. Imported palm oil moved up from 277/278 rupees to 280/281 rupees per 10 kg in the absence of fresh arrivals at the Bombay port and fresh outstation buying.
"Bulk buyers are lifting more edible oil now before the planned strike called by transporters next month. Buyers are trying to accumulate more stocks before this," one miller said.
Indian transporters are planned to strike next month to protest against the imposition of a service tax and hike in the insurance premium.
